clue.text: Loose favourite — French one comes first

indicators.note: says the French word is placed at the front, before the other piece

parts.note: un is French for one
a pick is a chosen favourite, as in 'pick of the bunch'

explanation.surface: A tipster names a loose-limbed favourite, with a French runner placed first in the race.
explanation.definitionFit: To loose a knot or seam is to undo its stitches, which is the verb's meaning of unstitching.

clue.text: Except when cloudy, going topless

indicators.note: the word loses its top letter, its first in a down answer

parts.note: a cloudy day is sunless

explanation.surface: A forecast: no sunbathing topless unless it turns cloudy.
explanation.definitionFit: The conjunction means 'except if' or 'except on condition that'.

clue.text: One's not at all clear or sure — a pope should clarify

indicators.note: making things clear is presented as rearranging these letters into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Someone unsure of a doctrine says the Pope should clarify it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's' reads as 'one is', so the definition is a thing that is not clear: a thick fog.
explanation.definitionFit: A pea-souper is a dense yellowish London fog, through which nothing is clear.

clue.text: Lord's house briefly seen as nicest in the middle

definitions.text: Lord's house briefly seen as nicest in the middle

parts.words: Lord's house briefly seen as nicest in the middle
parts.note: the established church, a house of the Lord, is shortened to three letters C of E, and the middle of nicest is C E, the two central letters, so 'C of E' is literally what sits in the middle of the word

explanation.surface: A churchgoer thinks the Lord's house the nicest building in the town centre.
explanation.walkthrough: The abbreviation is C of E; the two central letters of 'nicest' are C and E, so the short form is read as 'C of E' in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: The national established Protestant church in England, a house of worship for the Lord.

clue.text: Publicises cruise, possibly landing here?

parts.note: to air views is to publicise them, so airs means publicises
a cruise is a trip by sea

explanation.surface: A travel company advertises a cruise, wondering where passengers might land.
explanation.definitionFit: A strip of ground where aircraft touch down, the place a plane would come in to land.

clue.text: Eye part of Dublin, maybe avoiding hotel

indicators.note: the letter for hotel is left out of the word

parts.note: Dublin is an example of something Irish
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A tourist sees part of Dublin while avoiding the hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: The coloured ring around the pupil is a part of the eye.

clue.text: Perhaps Plato's classes shared opinions

definitions.meaning: Plato's Academy is an example of a school of philosophy, taken literally as the classes of a thinker
a set of views held in common by a group

explanation.surface: Plato's students all shared the same opinions.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a body of shared views, and literally a place where thinking is taught.

clue.text: Articulated beams put up

indicators.note: articulated means spoken out, so the word is given by how it is pronounced

parts.note: rays are beams of light

explanation.surface: Jointed beams are lifted into place on a building site.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise something is to lift it or erect it.

clue.text: Drama opening, bypassing a southern city

indicators.note: the drama word goes round the letter a, missing it out

parts.note: a play is a drama
a mouth is an opening, as of a cave or river

explanation.surface: A drama's opening night skips one southern city on tour.
explanation.definitionFit: Plymouth is a port city in Devon, on England's south coast.

clue.text: Distance made by set of clubs?

definitions.meaning: an old measure of distance, roughly three miles
a group of sports clubs competing against each other, as in football

explanation.surface: A golfer gauges how far a shot goes by the set of clubs chosen.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an old unit of length and an association of teams playing a season.

clue.text: May 1, lucky to be unoccupied? Very!

parts.note: might is a near-synonym of may, as in 'it may/might rain'
the digit one written as the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: an unoccupied word has its inside emptied, leaving only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone hopes the first of May will be lucky and the place quiet, and agrees emphatically.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are intensifying adverbs meaning to a great degree, extremely.

clue.text: Eastern sierra — wild scene for nature

parts.note: S is sierra in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A wild scene in an eastern mountain range shows nature at its rawest.
explanation.definitionFit: The essence of something is its fundamental character or intrinsic nature.

clue.text: Son using which method to lead trial presentation?

indicators.note: says the first pieces go in front of the word for trial

parts.note: how asks by which method something is done
a case is a legal trial in court

explanation.surface: A lawyer's son asks which approach to take in leading a trial's presentation.
explanation.definitionFit: A showcase is a setting for displaying something to best advantage, a display or exhibition.

clue.text: Thrown back from seashore, lobsters dance

indicators.note: Thrown back says the hidden letters are read backwards
from says the letters are taken out of the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Lobsters caught on the shore are thrown back into the sea, as if dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' signals the letters are taken from inside 'seashore, lobsters'; 'Thrown back' turns them round.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spanish dance in triple time, famously the subject of Ravel's orchestral piece.

clue.text: Expand chest, prepared to limit time on run

indicators.note: the rearranged letters hold the others within their bounds
prepared means made ready, so the letters are put into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece sits on top of the other

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: An athlete expands the chest, preparing to keep to time on a run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' rearranges CHEST into SETCH, which 'to limit' wraps round TR.
explanation.definitionFit: To stretch something is to make it larger or longer by pulling, so to extend it.

clue.text: Expert handling turnover in the cinema?

definitions.text: Expert handling turnover in the cinema?

parts.words: Expert handling turnover in the cinema?
parts.note: turnover suggests business takings, but it is the reels of film turning over in the projector booth, handled by the person who runs it

explanation.surface: A finance expert manages a cinema's turnover.
explanation.definitionFit: The cinema worker who operates the projector, handling the reels as they turn.

clue.text: Disgruntled six-footer follows quarry entering pub

indicators.note: the insect comes after the rest
the dig word goes inside the pub word

parts.note: an inn is a pub
to quarry is to dig
an ant is an insect, with six legs

explanation.surface: A disgruntled tall man follows a quarry worker into the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'six-footer' suggests a tall person but means an insect with six feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Indignant means angered by something felt to be unfair, which is resentfully displeased.

clue.text: Bottom in Eton, I prepared to be disciplined

indicators.note: the bottom word is placed inside the rearranged letters
prepared means made ready, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: a bed is the bottom of a river or sea

explanation.surface: A pupil at Eton, the English private school, expects to be caned on the bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottom' looks like a body part to be caned, but here it is a river's floor; 'in' places it inside the anagram signalled by 'prepared'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone obedient does as told, compliant and well trained in behaviour.

clue.text: Thickset like a St Bernard rescue dog?

definitions.meaning: stocky with a broad, deep chest

definitions.text: like a St Bernard rescue dog?
definitions.meaning: Alpine rescue dogs are pictured with a small barrel of brandy hung at the chest

explanation.surface: A burly St Bernard mountain rescue dog is described.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means broad-bodied and stout, and literally fits a dog carrying a cask at its front.

clue.text: More than one standard is about trade

indicators.note: the two letters go round the trade word

parts.note: to deal is to trade

explanation.surface: A trade negotiator insists on more than one standard.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideals are standards of perfection, and the plural form matches 'more than one'.

clue.text: Bear caught in Welsh river flood

indicators.note: the word for bear is held inside the river's name

parts.note: the Dee rises in Wales and flows to the sea near Chester
to lug something is to carry or bear it

explanation.surface: A bear is trapped when a Welsh river floods.
explanation.definitionFit: A deluge is an overwhelming flood or downpour of water.

clue.text: Runner-up? Nearer being a non-starter

indicators.note: the word loses its starting letter

parts.note: closer means nearer

explanation.surface: A runner finishing second was nearer but never really in contention.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner-up has lost the contest, coming short of first place.

clue.text: Terrible event, perhaps — in fact good, strangely

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are arranged in a strange new order

explanation.surface: Someone claims a terrible event was, oddly enough, good in fact.
explanation.definitionFit: A natural disaster beyond human control, such as an earthquake, is the legal phrase's meaning; 'perhaps' marks it as an example.

clue.text: Compete with conviction

parts.note: to vie is to compete

explanation.surface: Someone competes with real conviction.
explanation.definitionFit: A view is an opinion or belief firmly held.

clue.text: Taking a sample round, traffic it at Scene, feeling high

indicators.note: turned round, the extracted letters are read backwards
a sample is a small part taken from the whole, so the letters come from inside these words

explanation.surface: A drug dealer passes a sample around a busy scene, everyone high.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecstatic means overwhelmed with joy, elated, on a high; there is also a nod to the drug.

clue.text: Lizard King mural — neat, but odd bits missing

indicators.note: dropping the odd-numbered letters leaves the second, fourth, sixth and so on

explanation.surface: A mural of a Lizard King looks neat, though some odd bits are missing.
explanation.definitionFit: A large tropical American reptile with a crest along its back, one kind of lizard.

clue.text: Refuse to reduce volume

definitions.meaning: to reject an offer or request
to lower the sound on a radio or similar

explanation.surface: Someone declines to lower the volume of their music.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to decline an offer and to lower a dial's setting.

clue.text: Standing figures with no energy

indicators.note: the symbol for energy is taken away from the figures

parts.note: statues are carved or cast figures
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Figures stand still, lacking any energy.
explanation.definitionFit: One's standing is one's position or rank in society.
